transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I came in because... well, my mind just keeps going blank at the worst possible times. I'll be at work, looking at the road-closure forms or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps. And I've done this job for years. It's like the thoughts just stop.
What do you notice feeling emotionally right before your mind goes blank?

I don't really know. I haven't noticed any specific feeling right before it happens. It's just... I'll be standing there, and then everything is just gone. I'm not sure if I feel anything at all, honestly. It just happens.
When your mind goes blank, do you feel detached from yourself or as if the situation around you is unreal?

No, not really. I don't feel disconnected from my body or like things are fake, if that's what you mean. I'm still right there on the road, holding my sign and looking at the cars... it's just that the thoughts themselves disappear. Everything around me seems normal, I just suddenly don't know what I'm supposed to be doing.
Do these episodes of your mind going blank happen outside of work as well?

Yeah, it does happen at home sometimes. But... like I said when I first sat down, it's really the work situations that brought me in today. It just hits at the absolute worst times. I'll be staring right at those road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and I suddenly just cannot remember the steps to do a job I've done for years. So, yes, it happens outside of work too, but having my mind go completely blank like that on a live road is what really scares me.
When did these episodes of your mind going blank first begin?
It's been... well, it's been going on for about a year and eight months now. I noticed it started right after my closest friend passed away.
Since your friend died, have you experienced persistent longing for them or frequent thoughts focused on their death?

No, not really. I mean, I miss her, of course. We were close. But I don't sit around constantly wishing she was still here or obsessing over how she died. It was sad, and it hit me hard when it happened, but I'm not consumed by thoughts of her passing. It's just that the timing of these blank spells seemed to start right around then.
Before your friend died, had you already been having these episodes of your mind going blank?

No, not that I can remember. I really didn't have any issues like this before she passed away. My memory and my focus were fine back then. It wasn't until after she died that I started noticing my mind just... shutting off like it does now.
Since your friend died, have you felt sad or hopeless most of the day on most days?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness in my chest. It just feels like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor. And that feeling usually just stays with me for most of the day.
Since your friend died, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still try to do the things I usually do. I still read a bit, and I like to work in my garden when the weather is nice. I haven't really stopped doing those things or lost interest in them. It's just that I feel so down while I'm doing them now.
Since your friend died, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or thoughts of killing yourself?

Yeah. I just... I don't have the energy to fight the thought anymore that it might be better if I just didn't wake up. And I know that scares my family, because lately I've actually started saying it out loud to them.
Since your friend died, have you noticed any change in your sleep?
No, not really. My sleep has been about the same as usual. I haven't noticed any big changes with it.
Since your friend died, have you felt unusually tired or lacking energy most days?
No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I still get up and do my job as a crossing guard, and I get through the day okay. I don't feel any more tired than usual.
Since your friend died, have you noticed any change in your appetite?

Yeah, I have. Food just... it has stopped meaning much to me. I end up skipping meals without even really noticing. I only realize it because my work pants, my flagger pants, are getting pretty loose on me, and my family has started asking why I look so drawn lately.
Since your friend died, have you felt worthless or excessively guilty most days?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep replaying every little thing I failed to do for my friend. And not just her, but for the choir, and my own family, too. I really just feel like I'm a completely useless person right now, and... I honestly feel like I deserve whatever punishment is coming my way for all of it.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your ability to do your job and manage your usual daily activities?

I know I said earlier that I still get up and go to work, but honestly... it has interfered a lot. I've stopped being reliable once I'm actually there. I just couldn't finish the road-closure paperwork, and I started realizing I couldn't even trust myself with the basic traffic-safety steps out on the road. 

And outside of work, I've just pulled away from everything. I stopped going to choir, I stopped my volunteering, and I completely pulled away from my family, too. It really just got to the point where they felt they had to bring me in to get help.
